title: Firehall Supreme Pizza
subtitle: Pepperoni, sausage, peppers, mushrooms
description: Pepperoni, sausage, peppers, mushrooms. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Prep and sauté vegetables
steps.instruction: Sauté peppers, onion, and mushrooms in a dry-hot skillet 8 minutes until moisture evaporates — wet veg steams supreme pies. Brown sausage crumbles separately and drain grease.

steps.title: Preheat stone to 500°F
steps.instruction: Heat stone or steel at 500°F at least 40 minutes. Portion all toppings in bowls so the line moves fast — supreme night is a topping sprint.

steps.title: Stretch four loaded rounds
steps.instruction: Stretch dough to 12–14 inches. Sauce evenly with a ½ inch clean rim. First layer: half the mozzarella. This locks toppings so they do not slide off in the peel jiggle.

steps.title: Layer meats, veg, cheese, pepperoni
steps.instruction: Add sausage, peppers, onions, mushrooms, olives, remaining mozzarella, and pepperoni. Sprinkle oregano. Firehall Supreme means every slice has something — distribute, don't dump in the middle.

steps.title: Bake until loaded center sets
steps.instruction: Bake 12–15 minutes until cheese is browned at edges and the center is fully set — loaded pies need the longer end of the range. Rotate once. If center looks wet, give 2 more minutes; soggy supreme disappoints the hall.

steps.title: Parmesan, rest, and crew cut
steps.instruction: Rest 3 minutes, parmesan, cut 8 slices per pie. Fan on sheet trays for the line. Keep backup pie at 200°F on a rack — stacked boxes soften the crust.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up Firehall Supreme Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Pepperoni, sausage, peppers, mushrooms. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
